Natural-language requests go to central Secretary coordinator for understanding, planning and delegation to domain agents, each with independent context and self-review before tool calls. Goal: reduce copying information among expense, reminder, task and learning tools, retain context and return decisions to the user.

Cabinet / CabinetAI information architecture 页面: Today shows current tasks, pending approvals and sourced attention items, grouping reminders and tasks with near-due items first. Ask is the bottom full-screen conversation entry, expanding schedule/expense/learning/approval workspaces as needed. Cabinet at top right contains materials, memories and business records. Settings at top left covers privacy, device data, theme and language.

Cabinet / CabinetAI five agents 能力: EXPENSE Chancellor records and categorizes expenses and handles budgets in natural language; REMINDER Private Secretary offers time-confirmation cards, changing time, copying to system Reminders, undo and FCM push; TASK Delivery handles to-dos and deadlines. Secretary coordinates, rather than a single agent owning all domains.

Cabinet / CabinetAI KNOWLEDGE Provost RAG 知识 引用: imports TXT and PDF, including scanned PDF transcription by a vision model; retrieval-augmented answers cite original paragraphs and state missing evidence when material is insufficient. MEMORY Archivist uses Mem0 for long-term preferences and facts; users can inspect, correct and delete them, and deleted content must disappear from both retrieval paths.

Cabinet / CabinetAI extensions 行程 天气 照片 语音: implemented/production-or-validated capabilities in the supplied analysis include research then day-by-day itinerary cards, attraction images and per-day map switching (Shanghai three-day example; one simulator generation took 20.39 seconds, not a production latency percentile). Cabinet / CabinetAI device capabilities V1 设备 日历 健康 审批: reported live 2026-10-27, reads system calendar, reminders and health data (activity, sleep, heart rate). Calendar/reminder changes are proposals and execute only after the user clicks Apply. One change has one button; multiple changes or any deletion require item selection; deletion items default unchecked. AI privacy consent is required before sending to AI; data deletion/account management do not require AI.

Cabinet / CabinetAI reliability 可靠性 幂等 重试 时区: product principles reflected in code/acceptance criteria: clarify ambiguous dates; never report unsupported success (no article body means not collected, disconnected calendar means not rescheduled, heard does not mean mastered). Preserve successful partial results and retry only failed parts; idempotent submissions and double approval execute once; invalidate stale approvals when underlying data changes. External actions require approval by default; V1 excludes payments/transfers/purchases. Reminder ordering uses account-local calendar date; four timezones and daylight-saving transitions were validated. Principles/acceptance criteria do not establish every workflow passed real-provider end-to-end tests.

AI tools he uses: Codex, Claude, ChatGPT, Grok; has tried one more agent product (name unconfirmed). View: Codex suits architecture and product research; Claude suits deep coding, base frameworks and analysis. Frustrations: context too small or lost; switching between projects. Ideal assistant: one entry point, give it a goal and it decides the steps from history, with little human intervention.

Competitor view (his own): Meta AI and Gemini win because users don't switch tools; ActAI must remove a repeated hassle clearly enough to justify another app. In Cabinet he explored reducing copying, organising and manual steps after a user states a goal. Example: one voice message with a meeting time, materials and a deadline becomes a list to confirm, then the assistant carries on. Users won't drop WhatsApp at first; they adopt ActAI for one task, save steps daily, then move more conversations over. What matters is that going from saying it to getting it done is natural, fast and reliable.

Privacy view: users fear something said privately being used where they didn't expect (e.g. a private chat about changing jobs surfacing in a message the AI drafts to a colleague); that breaks trust even without a leak. Consent is not a one-time signup tick: users should see which chats AI can read and what is kept, and withdraw any time; deleted memories never come back; actions affecting others (sending, sharing) need confirmation of content and recipient; clear boundaries, user stays in control.

Why not a big company: not against big companies; at Kezhi's startup team he found he likes learning new tech around a real problem and building it into a product (Android and RAG in parallel); CabinetAI is his way of learning and validating new tech outside work; ActAI's communication focus is close to that. Draw: startup way of working plus product fit; wants a product he will stay with long term.

Testing and releases: at Kezhi he was the only Android engineer and also handled testing and releases; he built the whole Android app alone, from zero to launch, in four weeks (2026-11-12 user-confirmed; AI coding tools were weak then, so almost all code was hand-written; backend, web and iOS were others' work). At KKday he validated changes with data (SKU example).

Interviewing: took part in technical interviews when hiring engineers at Kezhi and KKday; focuses on what the candidate personally owned and follows one real problem: how they judged it, why that option, how they verified the result.

Real manager feedback (KKday Tour team lead): keep the scope of a change under control. Once a feature could be built on the existing architecture with more code, and he wanted to improve the related architecture at the same time to ease future work, which added time to that release. Lesson: long-term improvements need the right timing; now he presents the feature and the refactor separately and agrees with the team whether to do both in this release.
